correctness.rationale: Reconstructed all six template triple-block embeddings with one old hole and fixed +1,-1 at two residues. For each n mod3 the complete phase multiset (hole count, fixed signed contribution) is independent of template; finite factors recur infinitely often, including after one-hole completion, ensuring each phase accesses genuine tail extrema despite initial shifts. Thus signed-factor extrema satisfy U(3m)=U_tail(m), U(3m+1)=max(U_tail(m)+1,U_tail(m+1)), U(3m+2)=max(U_tail(m),U_tail(m+1)+1), with opposite minimum recurrences. Balanced-ternary digit weight H_3 satisfies precisely these recurrence cases plus |H(m+1)-H(m)|<=1, giving U=H and L=−H by induction over all directive tails. Sliding neighboring windows changes ones count by <=1, so no intermediate Parikh count is skipped. Verified both peak families. Fresh independent six-template simulated word windows and H3 parity at lengths n<=70 gave 420 matching cases; finite tests are not used as all-directive proof.

value.rationale: Exact Abelian factor complexity is a standard natural invariant distinct from ordinary factor complexity. Determining the full Parikh spectrum simultaneously for an uncountable family with all possible hole completions demonstrates unexpectedly universal digit-arithmetic behavior, with sharp unbounded peaks despite ordinary factor complexity 2n. The triple-block recurrence is a structural theorem, not an arbitrary numerical slice or finite census.

final_claim: For every infinite directive over the six Stewart Toeplitz templates and either one-hole completion, the full length-n Parikh spectrum is the integer interval of ones counts from (n−H_3(n))/2 to (n+H_3(n))/2, where H_3 is balanced-ternary nonzero digit count, giving abelian complexity 1+H_3(n) and unbounded logarithmic peaks.
limitations: Applies only to six balanced ternary one-hole templates; no Parikh-class occurrence frequencies or other Toeplitz alphabets.
